about: Electronics' tools for agents (through Agent Link): name, what it does, its arguments as JSON Schema, its group, whether it changes the document.

kicad_import.description: Read a KiCad board into the document (.kicad_pcb, KiCad 5 to 9). The file is parsed here; KiCad is not needed. path (required): the full path of the file. It makes the board as a solid body "PCB <name>" from its Edge.Cuts outline and thickness. The cut-outs and mounting holes go through it. It makes each tall component as a box over its courtyard, a body each. The height of a component comes from heights { "J1": mm } given here. Else it comes from the STEP model of the footprint, where this computer has it. Else it comes from a Height property on the footprint. With no height known, no box is made, and noHeight lists the refs. minHeight (3 mm): components under it get no box. centre: true (default) moves the middle of the board to the origin; moved says by how much. centre: false keeps KiCad's own coordinates, with y turned up. name: the name of the board (the file's name when left out). The bodies are plain Part solids. Every import adds a new board and components. Delete the old ones (object_delete) before you import a changed file. The facts of the board (size, holes, footprints, edge connectors, the path of the file) are kept with the document. board_enclosure and pcb_order_package use them. Refused: path is not a file. Refused: the file is not a board that KiCad 5 to 9 wrote. Refused: no closed Edge.Cuts outline. A big board with hundreds of footprints takes several seconds. The answer holds: board (its label), size [x, y], thickness, copperLayers, holes [{ at, d, kind }], footprints (how many), tall [{ ref, value, side, height, from }], edgeConnectors, bodies, noHeight { count, refs, note }, openOutline, moved, step. edgeConnectors: the connectors that board_enclosure opens the walls for. openOutline: pieces of Edge.Cuts that join nothing. The answer of a changing call can also hold health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.
kicad_import.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f8f209 (moved to Workshop Electronics)

board_enclosure.description: Make an enclosure round a board that kicad_import read, placed round it where it stands. It makes two new bodies: the box and its lid. The lid is laid beside, printed top down; turn it over about X to put it on. board: the label of the board (you can leave it out when one board is imported). It puts a standoff under each mounting hole. The screw comes from the size of the hole, unless screw says M2, M2.5, M3 …. The standoff height clears the parts on the underside. The headroom clears the tallest part on top. standoff and headroom (mm) override them. It opens the walls for the edge connectors that kicad_import found. skip [refs] leaves some closed. openings [{ side: front|back|left|right, at, width, height, z }] adds more, as gen_part's board_box takes them. wall, floor, radius, lid, lip, clearance, gap (board edge to walls) and margin (round each opening): all mm, as board_box's. name: the label of the box. Holes take the fit calibration of the printer (fit calibrate). When none is kept, holes are made 0.2 mm big, and printerFit says so. Refused: no board imported yet. Use kicad_import first, or gen_part { generator: "board_box" } with the sizes by hand. Refused: several boards and none named. Refused: a name that is not an imported board. Refused: a value out of the range of board_box. Each call adds a new box and lid: delete the old pair before you make it again. The answer holds: board, bodies [box, lid], outside [x, y, z], standoff, headroom, standoffs { screw, at, diameter, pilot, pilotDepth }, openings [{ …, for: the connector's ref or "given" }], printerFit, sound { label: true|false }, openingHeightGuessed { refs, mm, note }, step. openingHeightGuessed: connectors with no known height got a 5 mm opening; give heights in kicad_import. The answer of a changing call can also hold health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.
board_enclosure.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f8f209 (moved to Workshop Electronics)

pcb_order_package.description: Package the fabrication files of a board for ordering. Nothing is uploaded, ordered or paid for: the person does that. files (required): full paths of the Gerbers, drill files, BOM and placement (CPL) files that KiCad's fabrication outputs wrote. They are sorted by kind. vendor: jlcpcb | pcbway | oshpark. The order sheet says what to upload where for that house. The size of the board comes from board (the label of an imported board). Else it comes from size [x, y] mm, else it is read from the outline Gerber. layers (copper), thickness mm, quantity. name: the stem of the files. It writes to the folder of the session: <name>_gerbers.zip (upload-ready), <name>_order.zip and <name>_ORDER.md. <name>_order.zip holds the Gerber zip, the assembly files and the order sheet. When kicad-cli is on the PATH of this computer, it runs KiCad's design rule check on kicadPcb. kicadPcb is a .kicad_pcb path; else it is the imported board's own file. It reports the check under drc { errors, warnings, unconnected, first }. Otherwise drc says why the check was not run: an order is not checked until it is. Refused: a path in files that is not a file. Refused: no Gerber among them. Refused: an unknown vendor. Refused: a board that was not imported. Changes nothing in the document. The answer holds: gerberZip, package, orderSheet (paths), vendor, board { size, layers, thickness }, files { kind: how many }, drc, warnings, note.
pcb_order_package.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f8f209 (moved to Workshop Electronics)

printed_channel.description: Cut a channel inside a body along a path, for a wire or a conductive trace. path (required): [[x, y, z] …], two or more points in document coordinates. Each point is at least the size of the section from the one before. An end on a face of the part opens there; it is carried 1 mm past the face. An end inside stops blind. Between its ends, the channel must stay inside the part. section { shape: round | square, size: 0.4 to 20 mm (the diameter or side; 2 when left out) }. Corners are rounded to bend mm: the size of the section or 2, whichever is more. A turn of over 170° is refused. fill: wire (default), filament or paint. fill wire: the channel takes the hole calibration of the printer. awg (10 to 40, 22 when left out) gives the diameter of the wire, and its copper resistance. It also says whether the wire fits with 0.4 mm to spare. fill filament also makes the trace as its own body "<body> trace" for a second material, unless trace: false. Its resistance comes from material carbon-pla | electrifi, or from resistivity Ω·cm. fill paint: the resistance comes the same way. The channel is written into the body as a plain shape. So the body must be a plain Part solid (Part::Feature). Examples: an enclosure from board_enclosure or gen_part, an import, a part_transform copy. A PartDesign Body or a parametric Part object is refused, naming the plain copy to make. FreeCAD would rebuild it and lose the channel. Refused too: the sweep fails; use fewer, longer segments or a larger bend. Refused too: the channel cuts nothing (the path is outside the part). Refused too: it leaves the part unsound; move the path off the faces it grazes. Face and edge numbers of the body change. The answer holds: body, bodies (the trace too), length mm, section { shape, size, areaMm2 }, ends [open | blind, …], bend, removed mm³, sound, conductor { fill, resistivityOhmCm, ohms, note, wire { awg, diameter, ohms, channelAtLeast, fits, note } }, printerFit, step. A printed trace reads several times higher across layers than the figure given. The answer of a changing call can also hold health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.
printed_channel.source: Agent Link for FreeCAD 1f8f209 (moved to Workshop Electronics)
